info.title: Omnibus API
info.description: The REST API behind every Omnibus client. The web app, the iOS app and the MCP server all use it, and a new client can too. ## Signing in `POST /api/auth/login` opens a session. Set `client_kind` to `ios`, `android` or `bearer` and the token comes back in the response body; send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer `. Leave `client_kind` out and the server sets a session cookie instead, which is what a browser wants. An API token (`omni_…`, from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`) works anywhere a session token does, and suits scripts. Some media, such as covers, audio parts and book files, gets loaded straight into an `` or `

get.description:
Answers without a session, so a client can probe a server address before signing in.
`time` lets a client measure its clock's offset before it stamps progress writes.

Names, dates and the last four characters of each live token. A token's secret is shown
only once, when it is created.

post.description:
Makes a long-lived token that authenticates as you, for scripts and integrations. Copy
`secret` from the response: the server keeps only a hash of it and can't show it again.

200.description: The new token, with its secret.

400.description: The name is empty or too long.

delete.description: The token stops working at once.

404.description: You have no live token with that id.

400.description: The name is empty or too long.

404.description: You have no live token with that id.

post.description:
Checks the username and password and opens a session. Set `client_kind` to `ios`,
`android` or `bearer` to get the token in the body, for an `Authorization: Bearer`
header; without it the session arrives as a cookie. Send `device_name` as well and the
session is listed under that name.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie, unless `client_kind` asked for a token.

400.description: `device_name` or `client_version` is too long or holds control characters.

429.description: Too many wrong passwords: the account is locked for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Ends the session the request carries and clears the session cookie. Signing out of a
session that has already ended still succeeds.

get.description: The account the request's session belongs to: its permissions and preferences.

post.description:
Creates a user and signs them in, exactly as `POST /api/auth/login` does. The first
account on a new server becomes its admin. After that, registration works only while an
admin keeps it open; `GET /api/auth/registration` says whether it is.

200.description: The account exists and is signed in.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie, unless `client_kind` asked for a token.

400.description: The username or password breaks a rule; the body says which.

get.description:
Whether `POST /api/auth/register` will accept a new account. An admin opens and closes
registration with `POST /api/settings/registration`.

Every live session on your account. The one making this request has `is_current` set,
since it can't be ended from here.

delete.description:
Signs that session out wherever it is. To end the session making this request, use
`POST /api/auth/logout`.

400.description: That is the session making this request.

404.description: You have no live session with that id.

get.description: The full-size cover image, in the format it was stored in.

304.description: The cover is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`.

404.description: No book has that uuid, or the book has no cover.

get.description:
The library's books, ebooks and audiobooks together. Without paging parameters the
response is the whole library, capped at 50,000 books: `X-Total-Count` holds the true
total, and `X-Total-Cap` appears when the cap cut the list short. Set `sort`, `dir`,
`limit` or `cursor` to page through it instead, following `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The order to list books in.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Where the page starts: the previous page's `X-Next-Cursor`. Needs `sort` and `dir`,
set as they were for that page.

parameters.name: formats
parameters.description:
Comma-separated formats to include, such as `m4b,mp3`. Older clients send this;
newer ones put a `format` clause in `filter`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Filter clauses as a percent-encoded JSON array, such as
`[{"field":"format","mode":"include","values":["epub"]}]`. A clause matches a book
when any of its values does, and a book must match every clause. Up to 16 clauses
of up to 64 values each.

parameters.name: exclude_formats
parameters.description:
Comma-separated formats to leave out, such as `cbz`: the formats the user hides
from their library view.

parameters.name: stack_series
parameters.description:
Fold each series of two or more books into one row and list the series in `stacks`.
`X-Total-Count` still counts books. Applies to a paged request only.

parameters.name: omit_description
parameters.description: Leave each book's description out, for a lighter page. Applies to a paged request only.

200.description: A page of books, or the whole library.

X-Hidden-Count.description: How many books `exclude_formats` left out. Sent on the first page only.

X-Next-Cursor.description: The `cursor` for the next page. Absent on the last page, and when the request wasn't paged.

X-Total-Cap.description: The cap, sent when it cut an unpaged response short.

400.description: A `cursor` came without `sort` and `dir`, or a `cursor` or `filter` is malformed.

get.description:
The cover as a WebP thumbnail, `sm` (160×240), `md` (320×480) or `lg` (640×960). A
thumbnail is made on first request: until it is ready, which takes seconds, the full
cover stands in for it, marked to be cached for only a few seconds.

200.description: The thumbnail, or the full cover while the thumbnail is being made.

202.description: The book has no cover, so there is no thumbnail to make.

304.description: The image is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`.

ApiTokenView.description:
One live API token in the management listing (`GET /api/auth/api-tokens`).
Never carries the secret — that appears exactly once, in
[`CreateApiTokenResponse::secret`].

last_used_at.description: `None` until the token first authenticates a request.

suffix.description:
Last 4 characters of the raw token, for the `omni_…xxxx` display
identifier. `None` on tokens minted before the suffix was recorded.

BookFileInfo.description:
One `book_files` row — a single physical file on disk. Exposed to the
frontend so the format switcher can offer a file picker when N > 1.

duration_seconds.description:
Playing time of this file, summed over its parts. Present for audio rows only,
so never guess an audiobook's runtime from elsewhere.

Whole seconds, unlike the fractional `ProgressRecord::total_duration_seconds`:
a catalog row is read for "how long is it", not for position arithmetic.

etag.description:
Content validator for this file (see [`crate::file_etag`]). An offline client
snapshots it at download time and compares it with a later metadata refresh to
learn its copy is stale. `None` for rows the scanner has not stat'd yet, so the
one-time backfill never reads as a content change.

path.description:
Library-relative path (`book_files.scan_key`, e.g.
`clarke/piranesi.epub`) — what the delete dialog shows so an admin can
see exactly which file on disk a row stands for. `None` for rows
predating the `scan_key` backfill.

size_bytes.description:
On-disk size of this file. Lets the per-file Send-to-Kindle rows gate
oversized EPUBs the same way the hero export menu does.

Contributor.description:
A contributor (or creator) with the optional OPF refinements: the MARC role
code (`aut`, `ill`, `edt`, `bkp`, `trl`, …) and the sort-key name.

`id` is the `authors.id` primary key, set when loaded from a m2m join and
`None` for contributors created by the EPUB parser before indexing.

CreateApiTokenResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`. `secret` is the raw `omni_…`
token, shown to the client exactly once — the server keeps only its hash,
so it is unrecoverable afterward. Deliberately does not derive `Debug`,
same as `LoginRequest`: a stray `tracing::debug!(?resp)` must not leak a
long-lived credential.

total.description:
Total FTS5 hit count *before* the server-side `MAX_BOOKS_RETURNED` cap,
set by the search paths so the web client can show "N of M results"
even when `books` is truncated. `None` for the full-library
(`/api/ebooks`, `rpc_get_ebooks`) responses, which surface truncation
via the `X-Total-Count` header instead.

EbookMetadata.description:
Parsed metadata for a single ebook file.

`cover_url` is a relative URL to `/api/covers/:id` when the book has a cover;
clients combine it with their configured server base. OPF
`<dc:contributor>` entries are merged into `creators` (creators first).

accent.description:
Cover-derived accent color. Opaque CSS color value extracted
during indexing. `None` means "no cover or extraction failed" —
the frontend falls back to the theme default accent.

added_at.description:
Row insertion timestamp from `books.timestamp` — SQLite
`datetime('now')` format (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, UTC, space separator).
Drives the "Newest Added" sort — distinct from `modified` (DC
last-write).

book_files.description:
Every `book_files` row on this book, one per file on disk, including ordinary
single-file books. Each row carries that file's content validator
(`BookFileInfo::etag`) for offline staleness checks; count rows per format
rather than reading emptiness as a proxy. Empty only on the list projection,
which does not join this table.

description.description:
Sanitized HTML. `None` on browse rows — `LibraryPage.books`, their stack
members, and keyset `/api/ebooks` pages sent `omit_description=true` —
which never carry it: absent there is not empty, so read the book's
detail for it.

epub_size_bytes.description:
On-disk size of the file the hero "Send to Kindle" would deliver (the
lowest-ordinal EPUB, else the PDF). `None` when the book has neither.
Drives the oversized-file gate on the email button — see
`kindle_email_oversize`.

genres.description:
User-assigned genres. Unlike `subjects` (which the EPUB OPF supplies
via `<dc:subject>`), no file format Omnibus reads carries a genre, so
this list is sourced entirely from `metadata_overrides` — there is no
scanned baseline to revert to and no canonical link table behind it.

has_cover_override.description: True when `cover_url` is a user-uploaded override cover, not the scanned original.

has_override.description:
True when user-supplied metadata overrides are active for this book.
The detail page uses this to show a "has overrides" indicator and
offer a revert action.

has_physical.description: Whether the book has ≥1 physical copy checked in (drives the physical badge).

isbn10.description:
Secondary ISBN-10, sourced entirely from `metadata_overrides` — no
file format Omnibus reads carries a distinct ISBN-10 alongside its
ISBN-13, so unlike `isbn13` there is no scanned baseline underneath
this one.

isbn13.description:
Primary ISBN-13: derived from whichever `identifiers` entry (in
DB-projection order, not original OPF scan order) has a scheme
mentioning "isbn" and a value that normalizes to 13 ASCII digits, or
a user override from `metadata_overrides` layered on top at read
time. `None` when neither source has one.

last_interacted_at.description:
Most recent moment *anyone* interacted with the book — rated it,
published a journal entry, changed its read status, added it to the
library, edited its metadata or cover, or checked in a physical copy.
Fixed-width ISO, so it sorts lexicographically. Drives the "Recently
Interacted" sort; `None` only for a book carrying no signal at all.

page_count.description:
Page count of the CBZ archive `/api/ebooks/{uuid}/pages/{n}` would
serve, so the comic pager can render a slider and map progress onto
page indices. `None` for an EPUB-only book, a malformed archive, or
a row not yet backfilled since being indexed.

print_pages.description:
User-supplied print edition page count, sourced entirely from
`metadata_overrides`. Distinct from `page_count`, the CBZ archive's *image*
count that drives a comic's page slider: this is bibliographic metadata about
a print edition and can coexist with it.

series_id.description:
Stable `series.id` primary key from the normalized DB. Set when the
book was loaded from a join; `None` for books not in any series.

unique_identifier.description:
OPF unique identifier (`<dc:identifier id="…">`). Used by the
frontend to construct `/books/:uuid` and `/api/covers/:uuid` URLs.

stacks.description:
The series folded into one row each. Absent unless the request set `stack_series`
and the page held a series of two or more books.

EbookPage.description:
One response of `GET /api/ebooks`: a page of books, plus the series it folded into
stacks when the request set `stack_series`.

Health.description: A running server's liveness and build details.

app.description: Always `omnibus`, which tells this server apart from another program on the port.

build_id.description:
When this server process started, in Unix milliseconds. It changes on every restart,
so a new value means a rebuilt server is up.

repo_root.description:
The directory the server runs from. Development tooling uses it to tell the servers of
two checkouts apart.

time.description: The server's clock in Unix seconds, so a client can measure how far its own clock is off.

version.description: The release, such as `v0.9.3`, or `dev` for a local build.

Identifier.description: A typed identifier from the OPF, e.g. `{ scheme: "ISBN", value: "…" }`.

LoginRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/auth/login`.

Deliberately does not derive `Debug`: the struct holds a plaintext
password, and a stray `tracing::debug!(?req)` would write it to logs.

client_kind.description:
Optional — when present, server issues a bearer session instead of a
cookie session and includes the raw token in the response.

LoginResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/auth/login` and `POST /api/auth/register`.
`token` is populated only for bearer (mobile) sessions; cookie sessions
return the cookie in a `Set-Cookie` header and `token` is `None`.

RegisterRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/auth/register`. See [`LoginRequest`] for
why `Debug` is deliberately not derived.

RegistrationStatus.description:
Whether self-registration is open; the body of `GET /api/auth/registration`
and `POST /api/settings/registration`.

RenameApiTokenRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /api/auth/api-tokens/{id}` — the row's Rename action.

SeriesStack.description: A series folded into one grid tile.

lead_uuid.description: The member standing in the result list; the stack renders in its slot.

members.description: Every member in the result set, in series order.

series_id.description: The series page to link, when one resolves.

states.description: One state per member on server pages; empty on client-grouped stacks.

SessionView.description:
A session row as shown to its owner or an admin (device & session
management). Never exposes the token hash — only enough to
identify and revoke the row. Shared by the self-service
`GET /api/auth/sessions` and the admin `GET /api/admin/users/{id}/sessions`.

client.description:
Human-readable name of the client holding this session — the registered
device's name for a native client ("Seamus's iPhone"), otherwise a label
derived from the captured `User-Agent` ("Firefox on macOS"). Derived
server-side so the raw header never reaches a page; falls back to
[`UNKNOWN_CLIENT`] for a session minted before migration `0088`.

is_current.description:
`true` when this is the session the request authenticated with. Only set by
the self-service listing; the admin listing always returns `false`, even for
the admin's own session. Enforcement lives on the write side: the self-service
`DELETE /api/auth/sessions/{id}` refuses (400) to revoke the request's own
session id.

SortDir.description: Ascending or descending sort direction for a [`SortKey`].

SortKey.description: Sortable axes exposed in the toolbar / table headers.

StackMemberState.description: The viewer's reading state for one member of a stack.

percent.description: Whole-book percent (0-100) from the ebook position, if any.

started.description: Opened in any format: a status, a percent, or a listening position.

UserSummary.description: Safe projection of a `users` row. No password fields ever cross the wire.

book_detail_scroll_stops.description:
Whether this user's book detail page uses the snap-stop marquee.
`false` — the default, and what a pre-0092 payload decodes to —
renders it as one continuous scroll.

display_name.description:
Presentation name other users see, or `None` to fall back to
[`Self::username`] — which stays the login and admin identity.

has_avatar.description:
Whether this user has uploaded an avatar. Clients render
`GET /api/users/{id}/avatar` when set and a monogram otherwise.

hidden_formats.description:
Formats this user hides from the landing All Books view — canonical
lowercase tokens (`"cbz"`). Clients pass it back as the listing
request's `exclude_formats`; empty means nothing hidden.

kindle_email.description:
Send-to-Kindle destination address, or `None` when the user hasn't
configured one. Non-secret — the user set it themselves.

share_stats.description:
Whether other readers on this server may see this user's stats page.
`true` — the default, and what a pre-0099 payload decodes to.

stack_series.description: Whether this user's landing grid folds each series into one tile.

bearer.description: A session token from `POST /api/auth/login`, or an API token (`omni_…`) from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`.

media_token.name: token
media_token.description: A bearer token passed in the URL, for media that an `` or `

session_cookie.name: __Host-omnibus_session
session_cookie.description: The cookie a browser sign-in sets. A server running without secure cookies (`OMNIBUS_SECURE_COOKIES=0`) names it `omnibus_session` instead.
